references.text: Moses commands that the law be placed beside the ark as a witness against the people, paralleling how Moses here is the one accusing them of breaking his commandments.
God commands Moses to write a song that will serve as a witness against the Israelites, which prepares for the role Moses plays as accuser in John 5:45.

Moses warns of a prophet whom God will raise up, and the message of this prophet is a demand; Jesus points out that Moses himself wrote about him, and that rejecting Jesus is a violation of Moses' testimony.
Moses urges the people to listen to the law and not add to it or take away from it, emphasizing that Moses is the authoritative accuser when the people break the law.
Jesus continues directly in the next verse to explain that if they believed Moses, they would believe him, since Moses wrote about him.

The text draws a sharp contrast between the law being given through Moses, but grace and truth coming through Jesus, which underlies the accusation against those who rely only on Moses without accepting Jesus.
